name: Trenbolone hexahydrobenzylcarbonate

lead:
Trenbolone hexahydrobenzylcarbonate is an ester form of trenbolone, a synthetic anabolic-androgenic steroid derived from nandrolone. It was sold as Parabolan and Hexabolan and is now no longer marketed.
Bodybuilders and athletes use trenbolone esters to build muscle and reduce fat, which changes physique appearance. Human clinical research is minimal; the published literature includes a case report of liver cholestasis in a bodybuilder.

paras: It is used in bodybuilding circles by injection as part of anabolic steroid regimens; details of use are not given here. It is discussed on bodybuilding and looksmaxxing forums, including debates over whether public fitness figures are natural.

A 2006 case report described a 21-year-old bodybuilder with cholestasis, jaundice and itching after using Parabolan, who needed liver-support treatment [2]. A cough fit after injection, known as tren cough, is also reported. It is a Schedule III controlled substance in the US, Class C in the UK and illegal for non-medical use in several countries [1].

chain: More muscle mass and a leaner look
angle.text: Users aim for greater muscle and less fat for a more muscular physique. Because of its legal and health status, it is discussed mostly in bodybuilding contexts.

lead: Trenbolone hexahydrobenzylcarbonate, sold as Parabolan and Hexabolan, is a long-acting ester prodrug of trenbolone, a synthetic anabolic-androgenic steroid of the nandrolone group first synthesized in 1963 [1]. It was once used clinically in humans and is no longer marketed [1]. Forum writers use the names tren hex, Parabolan, and trenbolone cyclohexylmethylcarbonate for the same substance [2].

For appearance, bodybuilders and athletes use trenbolone esters to build muscle and reduce fat, which changes how the physique looks [1]. Anabolic steroids as a class increase protein synthesis, muscle size and strength, and reduce muscle breakdown, and Wikipedia notes that most users in US studies are non-competitive men training for appearance rather than for sport [3]. The ester slows release after injection, so the compound is described as acting over a longer period than shorter-ester forms [1].

Published human research on this ester is limited to case reports, including a 2006 report of liver cholestasis in a bodybuilder [4]. Looksmax.org references Parabolan mostly as a name in disputes about whether fitness figures are natural [5]. Trenbolone esters are controlled substances in many countries [1][3].

paras: Bodybuilders and athletes use trenbolone esters for muscle building and performance [1]. The appearance goals described in bodybuilding communities are a larger, harder and leaner physique, particularly in the preparation period before a competition [6][7]. Such accounts are anecdotal and this article does not reproduce dosing or sourcing information.

T Nation members describe the compound as part of multi-drug programs that also include other steroids and growth hormone, and some posts name professional bodybuilders as users, which is the way the forum documents how Parabolan entered competitive bodybuilding culture [6][7].

The ester was once used clinically in humans and is no longer marketed [1]. Trenbolone acetate, a different ester, is used in cattle to improve muscle mass and feed efficiency [1]. One forum post attributes the original pharmaceutical product to the French company Negma and says no legitimate manufacturer has produced it for many years [8].

Trenbolone is derived from nandrolone. Esters are prodrugs: after injection, plasma lipases cleave the ester group, and the active hormone is excreted in urine as conjugates [1]. Wikipedia lists several esters of trenbolone, including acetate, enanthate and hexahydrobenzylcarbonate, differing in release time [1]. A forum glossary states that Parabolan (cyclohexylmethylcarbonate) and trenbolone hexahydrobenzylcarbonate are the same substance, differing from enanthate by the ester [2].

Pharmacologically, trenbolone has anabolic and androgenic effects, increases muscle ammonium uptake and protein synthesis, and may increase appetite and reduce catabolism. It binds the androgen, progesterone and glucocorticoid receptors [1]. A popular claim that it is five times as potent as testosterone originates in a book by William Llewellyn; Wikipedia says this is unproven, with much data coming from rat studies, and that reviews suggest roughly three times the potency [1].

A case report describes a 21-year-old bodybuilder who developed itching and yellowing of the skin and eyes after Parabolan use, with a bilirubin of 65.5 mg/dl; he was treated with a molecular adsorbent recirculating system and recovered, with bilirubin 2 mg/dl at two months [4]. Tren cough, a violent coughing fit during or shortly after injection, is also described; Wikipedia says it is not specific to trenbolone and can happen with any oil-based steroid injected, with prostaglandins and bradykinin among proposed mechanisms [1].

For anabolic steroids as a class, Wikipedia lists unfavorable cholesterol changes, high blood pressure, left ventricular hypertrophy and increased risk of heart attack, stroke and sudden death; acne, hair loss, testicular shrinkage and, for aromatizable steroids, gynecomastia; liver damage with high-dose oral forms; and mood changes including aggression in a minority of users [3]. A small study of bodybuilders found focal segmental glomerulosclerosis in 9 of 10 users, and the IARC lists anabolic steroids as probably carcinogenic to humans (Group 2A) [3]. Steroids suppress gonadotropin release in a dose-dependent way, with testicular atrophy, reduced sperm production and infertility among the consequences [3].
A T Nation thread titled around the health of long-time tren users shows users themselves discussing long-term health concerns [9].

Trenbolone is Schedule III in the United States and Schedule IV in Canada, Class C in the UK (with no penalty for personal possession), Class C5 in Brazil, and possession or use without a prescription is a crime in Australia. Non-medical use is illegal in the US and several European and Asian countries [1]. Where steroids are controlled, a black market exists with smuggled, clandestine and counterfeit products [3].

Trenbolone acetate use in cattle has drawn research attention because of its metabolites. A 2013 Science study by Qu and colleagues found that metabolites degraded by sunlight could re-form at night, producing a daily cycle of endocrine-disrupting compounds; researchers nicknamed it the vampire steroid. Persistence in water can disrupt aquatic reproduction [1].

On looksmax.org the name appears in a thread about a YouTuber accused of not being natural, which reflects the natural-versus-enhanced debate in physique commentary rather than an instruction to use the drug [5]. T Nation, a bodybuilding forum, holds much longer discussion of trenbolone esters, including questions about muscle retention gained through anabolics and long-term health reports [8][9]. This article does not reproduce dosing, cycling or sourcing.

No controlled studies found. One case report describes drug-induced cholestasis after Parabolan use [4]. Research on trenbolone has otherwise been in livestock and rats, and general studies of anabolic steroids describe increased muscle size and strength [1][3].
